nodes.name: boost_9v
nodes.description: MT3608 boost converter generates VCC_9V from the global USB_5V rail for the NE5532 preamplifier supply only. EN is the available operating-mode control pin and should be configured for enabled operation unless a later system-level power policy is introduced. The FB path requires a passive feedback network added in downstream design to set the 9V output. This module is the sole provider of the internal VCC_9V rail and should be routed with attention to switching noise so the analog preamp supply return joins the common ground at the intended star point.

nodes.name: power_3v3
nodes.description: AMS1117-3.3 LDO generates VCC_3V3 from the global USB_5V rail for the digital control and DAC domain. This module is the sole provider of the internal VCC_3V3 rail used by the ATmega328P and MCP4725. Downstream wiring must add the required input/output bypassing. The 3.3V return path should join the common ground in a controlled way consistent with the analog/digital star-ground intent.

nodes.name: mcu
nodes.description: ATmega328P microcontroller provides digital control for the audio system. It is powered from VCC_3V3, with both VCC and AVCC tied to the 3.3V rail in downstream wiring, and uses the shared I2C bus on PC4/PC5 to control the MCP4725 DAC. PC6 is the only explicitly provided reset-capable pin and should be held in a valid reset policy by downstream support circuitry. This module owns the I2C master role and should define shared bus pull-up ownership in downstream implementation. Digital return currents should be kept local and joined to the common ground at the intended star point to avoid contaminating the analog audio path.

nodes.name: dac_gain_control
nodes.description: MCP4725 is a single-channel I2C DAC powered from VCC_3V3. It acts as an I2C slave on the shared control bus and outputs one analog control voltage on VOUT. The provided A0 pin must be set in downstream wiring to select the intended I2C address. Capacity note: only one DAC channel is available, so the design can implement only a shared GAIN_CTRL or bias-control signal for the stereo NE5532 stage, not independent left/right analog control. The DAC output should feed a passive control or bias network associated with the preamp rather than assuming a complete internal voltage-controlled gain function exists in the NE5532 itself.

nodes.name: VOUT
nodes.description: DAC analog output, rail-to-rail (0 to VDD).

nodes.name: VDD
nodes.description: Supply voltage (2.7-5.5V), also serves as DAC reference.

nodes.name: SDA
nodes.description: I2C data, open-drain. Requires external pull-up on bus.

nodes.name: SCL
nodes.description: I2C clock, open-drain. Requires external pull-up on bus.

nodes.name: A0
nodes.description: I2C address bit. VSS=0x60, VDD=0x61. Must not float.

nodes.name: stereo_preamp
nodes.description: NE5532 dual op-amp implements the stereo analog preamplifier stage. It is powered from the internally generated VCC_9V rail and common GND, using the dual channels for left and right audio paths. A shared analog control input from the DAC is exposed as GAIN_CTRL to support a passive bias-control or gain-shaping network added later; this phase does not require or assume a complete voltage-controlled gain circuit inside the op-amp. The module exports left and right preamplified outputs to the PAM8403 inputs. Because the NE5532 is in the sensitive analog path and is supplied from a switching-derived 9V rail, downstream design must emphasize local supply decoupling and analog-ground return routing toward the system star point.

nodes.name: speaker_amplifier
nodes.description: PAM8403 stereo Class-D power amplifier is powered directly from the global USB_5V rail and drives the stereo speaker outputs in bridge-tied-load form. It receives left and right analog inputs from the NE5532 preamp stage. SHDN and MUTE are the provided control pins and should be set in downstream wiring to a defined always-enabled playback state unless a later system control policy is introduced. The module exposes differential left and right speaker outputs as board-level outputs. Because this stage carries high switching and speaker currents, its PGND and signal-ground returns should be managed carefully and tied back to the common ground in a way consistent with the stated analog/digital star-ground intent.
